title: Universal scaling of the Anomalous Hall voltage of magnetic layer with the adjacent conducting layer
authors: Zhihao Yan, Qianbiao Liu, Zhengxiao Li, Lijun Zhu
abstract: The anomalous Hall voltage of magnetic heterostructures plays a key role as the indicator for the magnetization state and its interplay with a variety of spintronic effects. In this letter, we report the observation, mechanism, and impact of the universal, dramatic scaling of the anomalous Hall voltage of magnetic heterostructures with the thickness and resistivity of the nonmagnetic conducting layers (e.g., normal metal) by combining transport experiments, analytical derivation, and finite-element analyses. We identify that the mechanism is the serial resistor effect of the magnetic and non-magnetic layers within the magnetic heterostructures and irrelevant to any Fermi surface variation or angular momentum injection from the nonmagnetic layer to the magnetic layer. We also show that the accuracy of the harmonic Hall voltage analyses of magnetic heterostructures are unaffected by the under-measuring of the anomalous Hall voltage and other transverse voltages due to the serial resistor effect. These findings provide crucial information for understanding a variety of spintronic phenomena involving the anomalous Hall and other transverse voltages.
summary: This work analyzes how the Anomalous Hall voltage in magnetic heterostructures scales dramatically with the thickness of adjacent nonmagnetic layers. By combining experiments and advanced simulations, the authors prove that this scaling is governed by a simple serial resistor effect across the stack. This finding provides crucial insight into interpreting transverse voltages in spintronic devices.
main_problem: The study investigates the universal scaling of the Anomalous Hall voltage (V_AH) in magnetic heterostructures as a function of the thickness and resistivity of adjacent nonmagnetic conducting layers.
main_result: The dramatic scaling of V_AH is attributed to the serial resistor effect within the magnetic/non-magnetic stack, rather than changes in Fermi surface properties or angular momentum injection.
method: The research combines transport experiments (using lock-in amplification) with analytical derivations and finite-element analyses (FEA) to model current flow and electric fields.
model_or_system: The physical system is a magnetic heterostructure, typically an NM/magnet bilayer or trilayer. The analysis models the electrical circuit behavior using a serial resistor analogy.
key_observables: Anomalous Hall voltage (V_AH), harmonic Hall voltages (V_1\omega, V_2\omega), and the scaling dependence of V_AH on NM thickness (d) and resistivity ratio ($ho_{FM}/ho_{NM}$).
important_parameters: Nonmagnetic layer thickness ($d$), magnetic/non-magnetic resistivities ($ho_{FM}, ho_{NM}$), and applied electric field strength.
main_assumptions: The dominant mechanism governing the V_AH scaling is the serial resistor effect, which simplifies the analysis by decoupling it from complex electronic structure variations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the universal scaling of V_AH with NM thickness (Fig. 1), model current distribution effects (Fig. 2), and quantify the voltage reduction using the serial resistor model (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by presenting experimental observations of V_AH scaling, developing an analytical/FEA framework based on the serial resistor effect to explain this scaling, and finally demonstrating that other spintronic analyses (like SOT efficiency) remain robust despite this voltage reduction.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the rigorous modeling of transport phenomena using circuit analogies (serial resistance) provides a powerful, generalizable framework for analyzing complex interfacial electronic effects in nanoscale devices.
